title: The normalized finite compact-support compositor commutes with coefficient extension
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, a prime $\ell\ne D.p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ (in an independent universe), composable separated finite-type maps $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ of finite-type $D.k$-schemes, and arbitrary compactifications $c_f,c_g,c_{gf}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber; def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties; def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $S_f,S_g,S_{gf}$ be normalized coefficient actions [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action]. Suppose for each finite coefficient subfield $E\subset\Omega$ a natural isomorphism $A_E:Rg_{!,\mathcal O_E}Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}\simeq R(gf)_{!,\mathcal O_E}$ satisfies the proper/open normalization [def-zl-field-shriek-composition-normalization], and let $B_E$ be natural isomorphisms of the rational functors whose components are the raw localization of $A_E$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Transport $B_E$ along the literal finite-functor equalities in the three actions, obtaining $e_E:(S_fS_g)_E\simeq(S_{gf})_E$. For every inclusion $h:E\subset L$ and $K\in D^b_c(X,E)$, the scalar square commutes: $T_Z(h)(e_{E,K});\beta^{gf}_{h,K}=\beta^{f,g}_{h,K};e_{L,T_X(h)K}$, where $\beta^{f,g}$ is the canonical composite of the two action comparisons. This asserts only coefficient compatibility of supplied normalized compositors, not existence of the compositors or their descent.

proof.text: Apply the two-field integral compositor coefficient square to A_E, A_L and the three integralBeta maps, using hA and integralBeta_spec. This yields an equality of actual integral arrows for the one chosen field inclusion and input.

The rational scalar extension sends localization of an integral arrow to localization of its scalar extension (the coefficient-one specialization of its pure-tensor formula). The rational compact-support functor satisfies the same formula by LinearMap.baseChange_tmul. Relabel the three action functors by finite_eq; hB fixes the compositor components and rationalBeta fixes the three beta components. Rewrite the composite stage beta as bg followed by G_L(bf). Map the integral square through sfRationalConstructibleLocalization and use preservation of composition. Heterogeneous congruence for maps, components and composition transports this equality to exactly the stated stage-system equation.
